Section 2

Choosing the Right Solar System

An On-Grid solar system works in connection with the electricity grid and is primarily designed to reduce your electricity bills.

During periods when your solar system generates more electricity than you consume, the treatment of excess electricity depends on the applicable utility and regulatory arrangement.

A Hybrid solar system combines solar power with grid connectivity and battery storage.

It is designed for customers who want to reduce their electricity bills while also having the option of power backup during grid outages.

An Off-Grid solar system operates independently of the electricity grid and typically uses batteries to store energy for use when solar generation is unavailable.

It can be suitable for locations where grid connectivity is unavailable or unreliable.

The answer depends on your priorities.
• Choose an On-Grid system if your primary goal is to reduce electricity costs.
• Consider a Hybrid system if power backup is also important.
• An Off-Grid system may be suitable where dependable grid electricity is not available.

Not sure which one to choose? ADMA Solar can help you compare the options based on your actual requirements—not just the upfront price.

For safety reasons, a standard On-Grid solar system automatically shuts down when the grid fails. This prevents electricity from being fed back into the grid while maintenance or emergency work is being carried out.

If you need power during outages, a Hybrid system with suitable battery backup may be a better option.

In a Hybrid system, solar energy can be used to power your loads, while excess energy may be stored in batteries depending on the system configuration and operating conditions.

During a power outage, the battery can supply selected loads for a duration that depends on battery capacity and electricity consumption.

In many cases, yes—but this depends on the type of inverter and the original system design.

If future battery backup is part of your plan, it is worth discussing this before installation so the right equipment and upgrade path can be considered.

Expansion may be possible, depending on factors such as available rooftop space, inverter capacity, electrical configuration and applicable regulations.

If you expect your electricity requirements to increase, we recommend discussing this during the initial design stage.
Section 3

Cost, Savings & Your Investment

The cost depends on several factors, including:
  • System capacity
  • Type of solar system
  • Quality and configuration of equipment
  • Rooftop conditions and mounting requirements
  • Battery backup requirements, where applicable
The best solar system is not necessarily the cheapest—or the largest. It is the one designed to deliver the right balance of performance, reliability and value for your needs.

Your savings depend on your electricity consumption, tariff, solar generation, system size and applicable utility arrangements.

A well-designed solar system can significantly reduce the amount of electricity you need to purchase from the grid.

ADMA Solar can help estimate your potential savings based on your actual electricity usage.

The payback period varies from project to project and depends on system cost, electricity tariffs, energy consumption, solar generation and applicable financial benefits.

A solar system should be evaluated as a long-term investment rather than only on its initial cost.

We believe in clear, realistic projections—not exaggerated savings promises.

Yes, in most cases you may still receive an electricity bill.

The exact treatment of surplus electricity can vary by location and prevailing regulations.

Section 4

Subsidy, Approvals & Net Metering

Eligible residential consumers may be able to receive financial assistance under applicable government rooftop solar programmes.

Eligibility, benefits and processes are subject to prevailing government guidelines and requirements.

The subsidy amount, eligibility conditions and applicable limits are determined by the relevant government scheme and may change over time.

Our team can guide you on the current process and help you understand the requirements applicable to your project.

Yes. Where applicable, ADMA Solar can guide customers through the relevant process, documentation and installation requirements.

The final approval and release of any subsidy remain subject to the applicable scheme and the relevant authorities.

Net metering is a mechanism that allows eligible grid-connected solar consumers to account for electricity generated by their rooftop solar system in accordance with the applicable utility and regulatory framework.

The exact process, eligibility and settlement mechanism can vary depending on your DISCOM and prevailing regulations.

A suitable meter records electricity imported from and, where applicable, exported to the grid.

The adjustment or settlement of this electricity is governed by the applicable regulations and your electricity distribution company.

ADMA Solar can help you understand how the process applies to your connection.

The requirements depend on your location, electricity connection and the type of system being installed.

Depending on the project, this may involve documentation, technical approvals, meter-related processes and other requirements specified by the relevant authorities or DISCOM.

Timelines can vary depending on the location, documentation, utility processes and current workload of the relevant authorities.

While ADMA Solar can guide and support you through the process, certain timelines may remain outside the installer's direct control.

Documentation requirements can vary based on your electricity connection, location and applicable scheme or approval process.

Our team can provide you with a clear checklist based on your specific project.

Solar Performance & Everyday Questions

Yes. Solar panels can still generate electricity on cloudy days, although generation will generally be lower than on a clear, sunny day.

Yes. Solar panels continue to generate electricity during rainy conditions when sufficient daylight is available, although output may be reduced due to cloud cover.

Rain can also help remove some dust from the panels, though it should not be considered a replacement for regular cleaning where required.

No. Solar panels generate electricity from sunlight and therefore do not produce solar power at night.

At night, your electricity needs may be met by the grid or by battery storage in a suitably configured Hybrid or Off-Grid system.

Solar panels are designed to operate outdoors in varying weather conditions. However, very high temperatures can affect electrical performance.

This is why proper system design, equipment selection and installation practices are important.

A layer of dust or dirt can reduce the amount of sunlight reaching the solar cells and may affect generation.

Regular cleaning, based on local environmental conditions, helps maintain system performance.

Even partial shading can affect the performance of the affected panel and, depending on the system design, other parts of the array.

A proper site assessment and thoughtful panel layout can help minimise the impact of shading.

Yes. Many modern solar inverters offer mobile applications or online monitoring platforms.

Section 7

Maintenance, Warranty & Long-Term Support

Solar systems generally require relatively low maintenance.

Periodic cleaning of the panels and occasional inspection of electrical and structural components can help maintain reliable performance.

The ideal cleaning frequency depends on local dust levels, pollution, bird activity and rainfall.

Rather than following a fixed schedule for every location, panels should be inspected periodically and cleaned when necessary.

Solar panels are designed for long-term operation and typically continue generating electricity for many years.

Their output may gradually reduce over time, which is why manufacturers generally provide long-term performance warranties.

Warranty coverage depends on the specific equipment and manufacturer.

Solar panels, inverters, batteries and mounting components may each have different warranty terms.

Your project documentation should clearly specify the equipment supplied and the applicable warranty coverage.

The appropriate response depends on the equipment, nature of the issue and applicable warranty or service coverage.

ADMA Solar can assist in diagnosing the issue and guiding you through the relevant service or warranty process.

Our relationship with the customer does not have to end on installation day.

ADMA Solar aims to support customers with system-related guidance and assistance throughout their solar journey, subject to the applicable scope of service and equipment warranty terms.
